subject: Post-call: model shortlist + Redwood perf profiles & pilot ask
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@clearlens.ai>, Bob Patel <bob.patel@clearlens.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: model shortlist + Redwood perf profiles & pilot ask

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and concrete next steps so we all have the same plan.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: document summarization and question-answering over large legal filings (avg input 3k tokens, typical user prompt ~300 tokens).
- SLA needs: p95 latency <= 600ms for interactive UX, pilot run to validate production TPS.
- Data controls: KMS + optional VPC for pilot (you flagged legal/regulatory constraints).

Recommended model slate (shortlist)
1) rwdw-3-70b-q4f16 (quantized high-capacity variant) — best quality for long-context summarization
   - Redwood-verified TPS (512 token prompt, 128 token gen): 85 TPS on a 8xA100 dedicated pool
   - Latency percentiles (512/128): p50 120ms, p95 450ms, p99 720ms
2) rwdw-3-13b-int8 (cost-efficient contender) — good tradeoff for throughput-sensitive paths
   - TPS (512/128): 220 TPS
   - Latency percentiles: p50 40ms, p95 180ms, p99 320ms

Links: Redwood performance profiles and raw snapshot attached. Full perf pages: https://console.redwood.com/perf-profiles/rwdw-3-70b-q4f16 and https://console.redwood.com/perf-profiles/rwdw-3-13b-int8

Quality & regression note
- We flagged potential quality regressions on the domain-specific legal prompt set (sensitivity around named-entity handling and clause extraction). To mitigate we suggest:
  a) run our attached pilot_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (representative prompt/ground-truth pairs) against both variants
  b) enable A/B (canary) for 10% of traffic and monitor Rouge/F1 and hallucination rate thresholds
  c) add a regression guardrail job that alerts on model drift vs baseline prompt set

Pilot ask / next steps (proposal)
- Redwood pilot (2 weeks): production-like capacity (dedicated 4xA100), run 3k synthetic requests/day + a small sample of live traffic.
- Deliverables: perf snapshot for your 512-token SLA case, quality report on pilot_prompt_set_v2, and a short ops runbook for switching model variants.
- Confirmers: if this aligns, can we schedule a 30-min kickoff Wednesday 12/2 or Thursday 12/3? I'll loop legal/infra for the KMS discussion once we confirm.

Attachments: pilot_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (prompt pairs), redwood_perf_snapshot_20261129.csv (raw TP/latency), mutual_action_plan_Clearlens.docx (MVP phases + owner matrix)

Thanks — kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
From: Alice Chen <alice@clearlens.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Patel <bob.patel@clearlens.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model shortlist + Redwood perf profiles & pilot ask

Thanks Kimberly — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) For the perf numbers you shared, can you confirm the load profile for the p99 numbers? I want to know whether those p99s come from steady traffic or a mixed-traffic burst test (we expect spikes during contract review periods).
2) For the pilot, can Redwood provide an optional KMS-backed key we can rotate on-demand? Our security team also asked about encryption-in-flight certs and audit log retention (30 days minimum).

We like the 70B shortlist for quality but would also want to try the 13B for a cheaper baseline. If you can provide a short A/B plan for how you'd route traffic and gate the roll (and the perf snapshot for the 512/128 case), we're good to proceed with a 12/2 kickoff.

On the perf pages link: I clicked the 70B profile and noticed a note about model fallback behavior under capacity constraints — could you confirm what the user-visible latency looks like during a fallback to a cheaper variant?

Best,
Alice

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 16:02 Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:14:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: model shortlist + Redwood perf profiles & pilot ask

Internal note / action items following Alice's questions: 

1) Marcus/Vivek: run an on-demand mixed-traffic burst test for the rwdw-3-70b-q4f16 profile with 512-token prompts and 128-token gens. Produce p50/p95/p99 under:
   - steady 200 TPS baseline
   - 2x burst (400 TPS) sustained for 5 minutes
   - spiky Poisson arrival (lambda tuned to observed contract-review bursts)
   Output: perf CSV + annotated trace (attach to Drive folder above). Due EOD Tuesday 12/1.

2) Neha: confirm KMS rotation workflow and audit log retention defaults for Private/Dedicated pilots. Provide a short note we can send to ClearLens security (30-day retention min + optional extended retention).

3) I'll draft the A/B routing plan (simple 90/10 -> 70/30 -> 50/50 gates) and include the user-visible fallback behaviour doc: when fallback occurs, we surface a 503/soft-fallback header and auto-route queries to the 13B variant with a <10% increase in median latency in our tests; we'll add a circuit-breaker threshold at queue depth X.

Attachments to send to customer after we have Marcus' perf outputs: pilot_prompt_set_v2.jsonl, redwood_perf_snapshot_20261129.csv, mutual_action_plan_Clearlens.docx (already drafted).

I'll schedule the 12/2 10:00am PST kickoff tentatively and include infra/security.

Thanks — kim
